summary: Metals and plastics experts also offered their perspective on the future of the United States-Mexico-Canada trade agreement during the Supply Chain Outlook event.

title: The Recycling Partnership names new CEO
summary: TRP says it chose Greg Saxon, former COO of ITAD company PedalPoint Recycling, for his expertise in recycling, packaging, procurement and circular economy skills. He succeeds founder Keefe Harrison.

title: Biochar is booming. Could waste fuel its future?
summary: Production capacity for the material, which is created by treating organic matter at high temperatures, nearly doubled in two years. The American Biochar Institute projects even faster growth by 2027.

title: WM, Amp, Reju celebrate expanded facilities
summary: Amp says it has nearly completed the ramp-up of its Virginia MRF, while WM celebrated its latest $110 million recycling and hauling campus in Colorado. Reju’s R&D site is open in Pennsylvania.

title: California blocked from enforcing upcoming ‘truth in labeling’ law
summary: Ahead of an October start date, a federal court has granted a preliminary injunction. The Flexible Packaging Association and American Forest & Paper Association reacted to the news.

title: Philadelphia to retain Reworld, add Republic Services for waste
summary: Local advocates had hoped to convince officials to end shipment of the city’s waste to Reworld’s municipal waste incinerator in Chester, Pennsylvania, but were unsuccessful. WM will also continue to contract with the city.

title: Hispanic Waste & Recycling Alliance offers ‘collaborative’ space for growth
summary: Part of NWRA, the new group aims to support job, language and career training and offer a space for innovation and business development for Hispanic and Latino workers in the industry.

title: Reworld municipal waste incinerator destroys 98% of PFAS in EPA study
summary: The results were better than expected for a municipal solid waste combustion facility. But researchers cautioned additional study is necessary, as conditions vary across such facilities.
